question: Why can exactly equivariant neural networks have worse optimization landscapes than unconstrained networks, even when the desired solution itself is equivariant?

key_findings.claim: An equivariant architecture is a fixed subspace of an unconstrained parameter space, but it can still retain hidden parameter symmetries that generate additional critical points and divide that constrained space into distinct basins.
key_findings.evidence: The paper combines the principle of symmetric criticality with a hidden-symmetry construction. Lemma 3.2 creates constrained critical points from hidden fixed spaces, and Theorem 3.3 gives codimension-one conditions under which such a space separates two minima.

key_findings.claim: The obstruction is tied to how the hidden-layer permutation representation decomposes, not merely to the presence of an input-output symmetry.
key_findings.evidence: Theorems 3.4 and 3.5 characterize when reducible transitive permutation representations create the relevant hidden fixed spaces, connecting representation structure to the existence of symmetry-induced critical points.

key_findings.claim: In the constructed S3 teacher-student ReLU example, the exactly equivariant slice has two minima separated by a basin boundary, whereas relaxing the constraint turns the inferior minimum into a saddle and permits a path to the global solution.
key_findings.evidence: Figures 5 and 6 visualize the two minima and gradient-descent basins after 100 steps at learning rate 0.1. The relaxation trajectory temporarily acquires equivariance error, then reaches an equivariant solution through a different hidden representation.

anchors.section: Figures 5 and 6, loss surface and basins

key_findings.claim: The paper establishes an existence mechanism, not a general frequency or severity estimate for optimization failures in practical equivariant models.
key_findings.evidence: The formal results require particular fixed-space and representation conditions, while the numerical evidence is a small exactly analyzable teacher-student system. No large-scale architecture, dataset, or prevalence study is reported.

method.core_idea: Analyze architectural equivariance as a parameter-space constraint and identify hidden symmetries that survive inside it, then compare constrained and relaxed loss geometry.
method.mechanism: Represent equivariant networks as fixed subspaces, use representation theory and symmetric criticality to derive extra critical points, and instantiate the mechanism in a two-layer ReLU teacher-student loss whose basins can be plotted exactly.
assumptions: Group actions are finite permutation representations with the specified transitivity and reducibility properties.
The loss is invariant and sufficiently regular for the symmetric-criticality arguments.
The teacher-student population loss is informative about practical finite-data training geometry.

techniques.role: Transfers criticality between fixed subspaces and the ambient loss.
Explains extra critical points not dictated by input-output equivariance.
Characterizes architectures capable of the basin-splitting mechanism.
Allows optimization to leave the equivariant slice and bypass a bad constrained minimum.

evaluations.setting: Two-layer ReLU S3-equivariant teacher-student population loss
evaluations.metric: Critical points, basin topology, and final loss under grid-initialized gradient descent
evaluations.result: The constrained space contains two minima with separate basins; relaxation converts the bad one to a saddle and allows convergence to the global equivariant function.
evaluations.baseline: Optimization restricted to the exact equivariant parameter subspace

limitations: The theory focuses on fixed subspaces of finite permutation representations and does not cover all equivariant constructions.
The tensor-product parameterization can contain functions outside the compared MLP class, complicating broader architectural conclusions.
Conditions under which relaxation converts a bad constrained minimum into a useful saddle are not fully characterized.
The only optimization experiment is a small synthetic teacher-student example.
failure_modes: Relaxation may introduce additional bad directions rather than a traversable escape path.
An optimizer may not exploit the saddle direction before noise or regularization moves it elsewhere.
Breaking equivariance can harm sample efficiency or generalization even if it improves training loss.
The identified hidden representation may be absent in a different group action or architecture.
reusable_insights: Audit parameter symmetries inside an equivariant architecture, not only its input-output symmetry.
Compare constrained and ambient Hessians to distinguish a true local minimum from a constraint-induced one.
Use a controlled equivariance penalty or staged relaxation as an optimization intervention, then measure whether equivariance is recovered.
open_questions: How common are symmetry-induced bad basins in modern equivariant vision, graph, and scientific models?
Can an adaptive penalty detect when leaving the equivariant slice is beneficial and restore the constraint afterward?
Which representation-theoretic quantities predict optimization difficulty before training?

competitive_landscape.title: Geometry of the Loss Landscape in Overparameterized Neural Networks: Symmetries and Invariances
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies continuous/discrete parameter invariances and landscape geometry broadly; this paper isolates hidden symmetries that remain after enforcing group equivariance and proves a constrained-basin mechanism.

competitive_landscape.title: Symmetry and Critical Points for a Model Shallow Neural Network
competitive_landscape.relationship: Critical-point analysis using neural parameter symmetries
competitive_landscape.difference: The earlier work classifies symmetry-related critical points in a shallow model; this paper contrasts an exactly equivariant fixed space with its unconstrained ambient model and studies escape by relaxation.

competitive_landscape.title: Relaxing Equivariance Constraints with Non-stationary Continuous Filters
competitive_landscape.difference: It builds approximately equivariant filters for better task fit; this paper supplies a loss-geometric reason why exact constraints themselves can create optimization barriers even when the target is equivariant.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving Equivariant Model Training via Constraint Relaxation
competitive_landscape.difference: The predecessor demonstrates a relaxation strategy empirically; this paper develops a representation-theoretic mechanism and exact toy landscape explaining when constraint enforcement can introduce minima.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Exact equivariance can introduce optimization obstructions through hidden symmetries, and temporary constraint relaxation can remove them without sacrificing an equivariant endpoint.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper proves sufficient representation-theoretic conditions and realizes them in an exactly evaluated S3 teacher-student landscape.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The mechanism is conceptually sharp and falsifiable, but its practical scope remains uncertain until measured across realistic architectures and groups.
